title: California's 37th Congressional District election, 2026
description: California's 37th Congressional District, covering portions of Los Angeles County including South Los Angeles, Culver City, Baldwin Hills, and View Park, will hold a general election on November 3, 2026. The top-two primary held June 2, 2026 narrowed a nine-candidate field to two Democrats: incumbent Sydney Kamlager-Dove and challenger Samantha Mota. The district is overwhelmingly Democratic, with over 62% of registered voters identifying as Democrats, making the general election a contest between two candidates of the same party. This is a safe Democratic seat; Kamlager-Dove has held the seat since 2023 after succeeding Karen Bass.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for this race. The district is considered safely Democratic (Cook PVI: D+34), and no competitive general election polling has been conducted.

candidates.name: Sydney Kamlager-Dove
candidates.summary: Sydney Kamlager-Dove is the incumbent U.S. Representative for California's 37th Congressional District, first elected in 2022. She previously served in the California State Senate (30th District, 2021-2022) and California State Assembly (54th District, 2018-2021), and was a trustee on the Los Angeles Community College District Board. Her legislative priorities have focused on racial equity, criminal justice reform, arts funding, and universal healthcare.

candidates.name: Samantha Mota
candidates.summary: Samantha Mota (born September 1998) is a community advocate and first-time congressional candidate who advanced to the general election as the second-place finisher in the June 2, 2026 top-two primary. She previously served as a Santa Monica Public Safety Reform and Oversight Commissioner and ran for Santa Monica City Council in 2022. Mota's campaign emphasizes working-class representation, defunding ICE, universal healthcare, tuition-free public college, and term limits for Congress.
